chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The woman is buried up to her waist, then the Imam throws and the people throw with small stones; and the man is not buried when stoned, except up to his loins.

key_terms.أحجار صغار: Small stones — the specification distinguishes this from large rocks, reflecting the procedural details of the punishment
key_terms.الإمام: Al-Imam — the just ruler or Imam who leads the execution of hadd punishments
key_terms.حقويه: Al-haqwayn — the two loins/hips; refers to the area around the waist and hips of a man
key_terms.رجم: Rajm — stoning, the hadd punishment for proven adultery under strict evidentiary conditions in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the procedure for rajm (stoning) — how are men and women treated differently?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the procedural distinctions in the execution of the hadd punishment of stoning (rajm). The woman is buried up to her waist before stoning begins, while the man is buried only up to his loins (hips). In both cases, the Imam leads by throwing first, followed by the general public using small stones. These distinctions were elaborated by classical jurists as reflecting both the modesty requirements for women and the practical mechanics of the punishment.
